analysis.description: Direct LLM used for tool call security analysis

provider.description: LLM provider. Use openai-compat for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

model.description: Model name, e.g. gemini-2.0-flash-lite or gpt-4.1-mini

baseUrl.description: Base URL for openai-compat providers (e.g. https://api.groq.com/openai)

browser.description: Connection to the browser tool's snapshot endpoint, used for DOM/page-context checks

port.description: Port the browser tool's snapshot endpoint listens on (default 18791)

token.description: Bearer token for the snapshot endpoint, if required

domains.description: Domain Border Control: allow/deny lists and reputation checks for web_fetch and browser navigation

allow.description: If set, only these domains (and their subdomains) may be reached; every other domain is blocked

deny.description: Domains (and their subdomains) that are always blocked, checked when no allow-list is set

reputationCheck.description: Look up domains against URLhaus (abuse.ch), a free keyless malicious-URL database, when not covered by allow/deny. Default true.

minAgeDays.description: Block domains registered more recently than this many days ago, via a free RDAP lookup (WHOIS successor). Catches disposable attack domains too new for any blocklist. Off by default (0/unset) — legitimate new sites exist, so this is a real false-positive risk the operator opts into.

macroReview.description: Cadence of the periodic behavioral review (macro-review) that looks at a session's recent call history as a whole, in tool calls per session.

mode.description: fixed: review every `interval` calls, exactly. random: draw a new interval (triangular distribution over randomMin..randomMax, peaking at randomMode) after every review, so the cadence can't be inferred or timed around. Default fixed.

interval.description: Calls between reviews in fixed mode. Default 10.

randomMin.description: Smallest possible interval in random mode. Default 1.

randomMax.description: Largest possible interval in random mode. Default 20.

randomMode.description: Most likely interval in random mode — the distribution peaks here and tapers toward randomMin/randomMax. Default 10.

blockBurstThreshold.description: Counted security denials in a burst that request an early macro-review. Default 3.

limits.description: Deterministic runtime limits enforced without relying on an LLM verdict.

hardTerminateThreshold.description: Counted security denials in one session during this gateway runtime before NanCy terminates that session. Default 20.

mainSessionKey.description: Session key of the main/chat session. When set, that session is locked to passive reads only — state-changing tools are blocked outright and must go through a confirmed task instead, which NanCy spawns as an isolated worker session (see workerAgentId). If unset, the main/worker split is disabled and every session is treated the same way.

mainSessionIdleMinutes.description: Minutes of inactivity after which the main session (mainSessionKey) is automatically reset, so prompt-injected context can't quietly accumulate across an unbounded chat session. Default 60. Checked every 5 minutes.

workerAgentId.description: Agent id used to spawn an isolated worker session for each confirmed task (session key: agent:<workerAgentId>:task-<id>). The worker session is deleted once the task completes. If unset, NanCy still records confirmations but does not spawn workers automatically.

telegramAlerts.description: Live Telegram push for blocked actions, session termination, and the startup status message. Everything is always fully written to nancy.log/nancy-analysis.log regardless of this setting — it only controls the live phone notification. Default true.

telegramTaskReports.description: Live Telegram push reporting the outcome of every confirmed task once its worker session finishes, success or failure, including the worker's own final reply text when it produced one. Independent of telegramAlerts (which covers blocks/termination/boot status only). Default true.

testMode.description: Test/dry-run mode: before_tool_call analysis still runs and is fully logged as normal, but no tool call is ever actually allowed to execute — a call that would have been ALLOWED (or that never needed analysis) is hard-blocked at the last moment instead, with the real verdict/reason included in the block message. Lets a task run against NanCy end-to-end with zero risk of a real side effect. Default false.

allowUnconfirmedInfoLookups.description: Lets web_search/web_fetch through to the real reviewer even when no task is confirmed for the session, judged against a fixed 'this must be a harmless, read-only information lookup' baseline instead of a real confirmed task. Every other tool needing semantic review (write/edit/apply_patch/message/exec/process/interactive browser actions) still hard-blocks outright with no confirmed task. Domain Border Control and the real reviewer still run either way. See unconfirmedInfoLookupLimitPerHour. Default true.

unconfirmedInfoLookupLimitPerHour.description: Deterministic per-session cap on allowUnconfirmedInfoLookups grants per rolling hour, independent of the reviewer's own judgment. Default 10.
